elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: § 16.1(A) warrants only that M&I's systems are "capable of performing the Services in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement"; no professional/workmanlike or industry-standard performance standard appears, and the inserted subsection adds none (indeed § 9.1's "no other or higher degree of care" language survives).

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: § 16.1(B): "The reports made available to Customer shall be in substantial conformity with the customer bulletins and the User Manuals" — the reports are the deliverable and the User Manuals/bulletins are the documentation.

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Insertion sets the express floor at "not less than ninety (90) days following delivery of each report" plus coverage "throughout the Term"; the Term's length is not in the rendered language, so a 12-month duration is not confirmable on the face of the operative text.
Insertion fixes only "thirty (30) days following performance of each Service" as the express floor, plus indeterminate "throughout the Term" coverage; a 90-day services floor is not stated.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Insertion: "M&I shall promptly repair or replace the non-conforming Services or reports".
Insertion: "or, at Customer's election, refund the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or reports".

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in §16.1(A)-(B), (F) or the inserted subsection; (C) rights, (D) authority and (E) Millennium Compliance do not supply it.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code / virus warranty in the cited warranty text or in the insertion.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: § 16.1(B) supplies documentation conformance for the reports (the software output deliverable in this service-bureau deal), and the insertion fixes it "throughout the Term and in any event for not less than ninety (90) days following delivery of each report".

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: § 16.1(A) is the Services warranty; the insertion gives it a period "throughout the Term and in any event for not less than ... thirty (30) days following performance of each Service".

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "For breach of any warranty in this Section 16.1, M&I shall promptly repair or replace the non-conforming Services or reports" — an operative remedy that did not previously exist (§ 12.3 gave only dispute resolution/termination plus Damages).
"or, at Customer's election, refund the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or reports".

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the single inserted subsection supplies the missing warranty period (90-day report / 30-day Services floors) and the missing repair-or-replace-or-refund remedy, attaching to the existing express warranties in § 16.1(A) and (B).

Not a walk-away: the § 16.1(F) disclaimer is expressly carved back ("EXCEPT AS SPECIFICALLY SET FORTH IN THIS SECTION 16.1"), and the insertion sits inside § 16.1 so it is not swallowed by the disclaimer.

Preferred level fails on four points the drafter did not press and would need to add to reach it: (i) a professional-and-workmanlike performance standard, (ii) a stated 12-month software period, (iii) a 90-day (not 30-day) Services period, (iv) compliance-with-laws and no-malicious-code warranties.

Minimality holds: no existing words are deleted or paraphrased, favourable language (Term-long, unlimited-on-its-face warranties; the carve-back in (F)) is retained by the express "shall remain in effect throughout the Term" savings phrase, and nothing outside the warranty period/remedy is touched. Two small drifts from model language are worth noting but do not defeat minimality: "promptly" and vesting the refund choice "at Customer's election" rather than at Vendor's option, which is stronger than the playbook model and is the likeliest point of pushback.

Intent preserved: § 12.3's default remedies, the Article 15 dispute path and the § 13.4 cap survive without contradiction; the period sentence is limited to (A) and (B) while the remedy sentence covers "any warranty in this Section 16.1", which is additive rather than inconsistent, and no cross-reference is left dangling.

Housekeeping: the rationale and comment describe the insertion as lettered § 16.1(G), but the rendered text begins "Warranty Period; Remedy." with no subsection letter — add the "G." designation so the numbering scheme of § 16.1(A)-(F) is not broken.
